card.text: Explore the measured nucleus of comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko from Rosetta.

introduction.text: 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko is the two-lobed comet explored by Rosetta. Rotate its measured nucleus to inspect the narrow neck, steep cliffs and recessed terrain.

model.title: Nucleus shape reconstruction
model.summary: Nucleus shape measured by Rosetta and simplified for display. The gray surface is a model material.

osiris.title: OSIRIS image mosaic
osiris.summary: Eight Rosetta photographs show cliffs, pits and smoother plains across both hemispheres. Grid marks gaps in the photography; original shadows and some seams remain.

albedo.title: VIRTIS single-scattering albedo
albedo.summary: How strongly surface grains scatter green light. Higher values mean more scattering. Turn Shadows off to read the color scale.

slope.title: VIRTIS visible spectral slope
slope.summary: How much reflectance rises from green to red light. Higher values mean a redder spectrum. Turn Shadows off to read the color scale.

absorption.title: VIRTIS 3.2 µm absorption depth
absorption.summary: Strength of the broad 3.2 µm absorption band. This measurement alone cannot tell us how much organic material is present. Turn Shadows off to read the scale.

ice.title: VIRTIS surface ice fraction
ice.summary: Estimated ice seen in reflected light, not the ice stored inside the comet. A value of 0% means the model fitted no ice. Turn Shadows off to read the scale.

regions.title: Named regions of 67P
regions.summary: Color separates the 26 named regions used to describe the comet’s terrain. These are geographical divisions, not different minerals. Grid marks places where the source maps could not be matched reliably to this shape.

geology.title: Geological features mapped from OSIRIS
geology.summary: Fractures, cliffs, terraces and small features mapped from Rosetta images. Lines and dots are map symbols, not their true widths or sizes. Grid marks areas outside the study or without a reliable shape match.
